headline: Sterling is about 1.34 dollars early on Tuesday, a touch lower overnight after reports of US defensive strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island lifted oil and the dollar slightly. Americans vote in the midterm elections today, the Bank of England decides on Thursday 5 November and US jobs figures follow on Friday 6 November.

drivers.title: Fed rate expectations
drivers.text: CME FedWatch put the chance of a Fed rise in December at about 75% on 2 November, according to FXStreet, supported by last Thursday's strong US figures and a firmer than expected US factory survey on Monday (55.5 against 54.5). Signs that keep a December rise in view tend to lift the dollar.

drivers.title: Oil and the Gulf
drivers.text: Brent settled 7.63% lower at $104.77 (about £78) on 2 November, its biggest fall since July, on hopes for US and Iran diplomacy, then rose 0.5% to $105.25 (about £79) in early Asian trade on 3 November after reports of US strikes on Qeshm Island. Dearer oil and Gulf tension tend to lift the dollar, and easing tension the reverse.

drivers.title: Iran talks
drivers.text: President Trump said on 2 November that a deal with Iran could happen and that Iran wants a settlement, and Tehran said contacts with Washington were continuing, though talks through Qatari mediators have produced no breakthrough. Hours later US officials described limited defensive strikes near the Strait of Hormuz. Each turn in these talks can move oil and the dollar.

drivers.title: The UK side
drivers.text: Bank Rate is 3.75%, and economists polled by Reuters expect a rise to 4% on 5 November, which would be the first rise since August 2023. Reuters notes the Bank may push back on the further rises priced for 2027. A rise that is already priced in gives the pound less of a lift than a surprise would, so the guidance from the Bank will count for more.

drivers.title: The midterms
drivers.text: US midterm elections are today, 3 November. Republicans hold the Senate 53 to 47 and the House 220 to 215, and betting markets gave the Democrats about a 70% chance of taking both chambers on 2 November; ING says a Democratic sweep could weigh slightly on the dollar through shutdown and debt ceiling risks.

lower: More US strikes on Iran or attacks on shipping that push oil higher, which would tend to lift the dollar as a safe haven.
Firmer US figures this week, such as job openings above 7.11 million today or a jobs number above 63,000 on 6 November, which would firm up a December Fed rise and lift the dollar.
A Bank of England that raises rates on 5 November but pushes back on the further rises markets expect, which would take away support that the pound already has.
A midterm result that keeps Republican control of Congress, against the betting markets, which would remove the slight dollar weakness ING links to a Democratic sweep.
higher: Progress in the Iran talks or on reopening Hormuz, which would bring oil down and tend to weaken the dollar.
A Democratic sweep in the midterms, which ING says could weigh slightly on the dollar through shutdown and debt ceiling risks.
A Bank of England that raises rates on 5 November and hints at more, which would lift the pound.
A US jobs number below the forecast of 63,000 on 6 November, which would make a December Fed rise less certain and weaken the dollar.
watch: Americans vote in the midterm elections today, with results coming through overnight into Wednesday in Dubai. US job openings come at 19:00 Dubai today (7.11 million forecast); a lower number would help someone selling pounds for dirhams and a higher one would hurt. The Bank of England follows at 16:00 Dubai on Thursday 5 November, where a rise to 4% is expected; a firmer message on further rises would help and a cautious one would hurt.

feed.title: Sterling has edged back up as the dollar eased through the Asian morning
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from an overnight low of about 1.3397 at 07:15 Dubai to about 1.3415 by 09:35 Dubai and was still near 1.3415 at 10:35 Dubai, leaving aside one stray trade at 1.3478, while EUR/USD rose in step from about 1.1182 to about 1.1193, which points to a slightly softer dollar rather than news about the pound. No report read names a cause for the drift: oil has held its small early rise after the reports of US strikes on Qeshm Island, and no further escalation has been reported. The Reserve Bank of Australia raised its rate to 4.85% this morning as expected, and the Australian dollar fell, so that decision did not weaken the dollar more widely.

feed.title: The dollar has firmed after reports of US strikes on Iran
feed.text: US officials told the Wall Street Journal and CBS News that American forces made limited defensive strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz, after Revolutionary Guard forces fired on a US aircraft, and Brent rose 0.5% to $105.25 (about £79) by 05:04 Dubai after falling 7.6% on Monday. Gulf tension tends to lift the dollar as a safe haven, and GBP/USD fell from about 1.3414 at 04:39 Dubai to about 1.3401 at 04:42 Dubai while EUR/USD fell in step from about 1.1192 to 1.1184, which points to the dollar, though no report read gives the exact time the news broke. Sterling has since held near 1.3400, a little below Monday evening's 1.3409, with an overnight low of about 1.3395.

feed.title: Sterling is little changed as oil slumps and US shares fade
feed.text: Brent fell 7.7% to $104.66 (about £78) on hopes for US and Iran diplomacy, and an Iranian report at 22:25 Dubai said the two sides were close to a preliminary agreement, although neither government has confirmed it. Cheaper oil and easier tension tend to weaken the dollar, yet GBP/USD fell from about 1.3419 at 21:50 Dubai to about 1.3402 at 22:50 Dubai, and EUR/USD fell from about 1.1204 to about 1.1190, which points to a firmer dollar. No report read names a cause for that step, though it came as US technology shares turned lower on selling in chip stocks. GBP/USD then recovered to about 1.3409, little changed from about 1.3415 four hours earlier, with a high of about 1.3422 and a low of about 1.3402 over that time, leaving aside one stray trade at 1.3431.

feed.title: Sterling has edged lower after a stronger US factory survey
feed.text: The ISM manufacturing index for October came in at 55.5 against 54.5 expected and 54.5 last time, while its prices measure fell to 75.2 against about 77.5 expected. Stronger activity tends to support the dollar by keeping a December Fed rise in view, but softer price pressure limits that effect, and investingLive notes that some of the gain came from inventories and slower deliveries rather than new orders. GBP/USD slipped from about 1.3421 at 19:00 Dubai to 1.3416 within three minutes, returned to about 1.3423 by 19:10 Dubai and was about 1.3414 at 19:38 Dubai, a small move, and EUR/USD eased from about 1.1212 to about 1.1196, which points to the dollar.

feed.title: Sterling has recovered part of its slide as oil stayed lower
feed.text: West Texas crude was down about 4% near $99.80 (about £74) on hopes for a US and Iran deal, although no agreement has been confirmed, and cheaper oil and easier tension tend to weaken the dollar. GBP/USD rose from about 1.3402 at 15:00 Dubai to about 1.3425 at 17:38 Dubai, then eased to about 1.3418. The last step came between 17:36 and 17:38 Dubai, when EUR/USD also rose from about 1.1210 to about 1.1220, which points to the dollar, but no report read names a cause for that step, and the US factory survey is still to come at 19:00 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has given back its morning gain as the dollar steadied
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from about 1.3444 at 13:15 Dubai to about 1.3405 at 14:40 Dubai, a drop of 0.29%, while EUR/USD fell 0.22% from about 1.1232 to about 1.1207, which points mainly to the dollar recovering, with the pound slightly the weaker. No report read names a cause for the slide. UK factory figures at 13:30 Dubai matched the first estimate at 52.8, so they were no surprise, and the fall had begun before them. Reuters notes the Bank of England rise to 4% on Thursday is widely expected and that the Bank may push back on the three to four further rises priced for 2027, which would weigh on the pound if it does.

feed.title: Sterling has touched 1.3444 on a weaker dollar, then given part of it back
feed.text: Investing.com says the dollar eased as oil fell 2% to 3% on reports that President Trump wants diplomacy with Iran to run its course, and that the pound's gain owes more to the dollar than to UK fundamentals. GBP/USD rose from about 1.3419 at 12:30 Dubai to about 1.3444 by 13:15 Dubai, and EUR/USD rose in step from about 1.1197 to about 1.1232, which points to the dollar. GBP/USD then slipped back to about 1.3423 by 13:40 Dubai and EUR/USD to about 1.1216; no report read names a cause for that pullback.

feed.title: The dollar has slipped further as the mood improved before the midterms
feed.text: US stock futures rose between 0.4% and 0.9% and West Texas crude fell about 2%, after a weekend with no US strikes on Iran and talk of a shorter timetable for reopening Hormuz, though Washington has not accepted that plan. Better risk appetite reduces demand for the dollar as a safe haven, and ING says traders may also trim dollar positions before Tuesday's vote. GBP/USD rose from about 1.3395 at 10:30 Dubai to about 1.3416 at 11:35 Dubai and EUR/USD rose from 1.1175 to 1.1187, which points mainly to the dollar, with the pound slightly the stronger; no report read names a single event behind the step, and no UK figure had come out.

feed.title: The dollar has eased as oil fell further on hopes for Iran diplomacy
feed.text: Brent was down more than 3% at about $110 (about £82) at 07:55 Dubai, after Axios reported that President Trump told Israel's prime minister he wanted to give diplomacy more time before any further strikes. FXStreet says optimism about a breakthrough is weakening the dollar as a safe haven, while the expected Bank of England rise is supporting the pound. GBP/USD rose from about 1.3389 at 08:55 Dubai to about 1.3401 by 09:20 Dubai and EUR/USD rose in step from 1.1167 to 1.1178, which points to the dollar rather than news about the pound.

feed.title: Oil has fallen on a two-day plan to reopen Hormuz
feed.text: The banks' market has reopened with sterling little changed: GBP/USD closed Friday near 1.3389, stayed between about 1.3373 and 1.3391 in thin weekend trading, and was about 1.3385 at 07:40 Dubai on Monday. Brent fell about $2 to about $111 (about £83) in early Asian trade after Iran's foreign minister said Qatari mediators had agreed a plan with Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days, if the US meets a list of demands; Washington has not responded publicly. Cheaper oil tends to soften the dollar, but FXStreet says the chance of a December Fed rise, about 75%, is still supporting it, and at least ten shipping incidents have been reported in the region since 31 October. No report read names a cause for sterling's small moves overnight.

feed.title: Sterling has given back part of today's gain as the dollar recovered
feed.text: US employment costs rose 0.8% in the third quarter, exactly as forecast, so that figure gave little reason to move. GBP/USD still fell from 1.3429 at 16:25 Dubai to about 1.3378 at 18:00 Dubai, and EUR/USD fell in step from 1.1188 to 1.1144, which points to a firmer dollar rather than news about the pound. No report read so far names the cause of the slide, which began before the Fed's Tom Barkin spoke at 17:30 Dubai; later, at about 20:30 Dubai, the Fed's Alberto Musalem said rates will need to rise again soon, which tends to support the dollar. GBP/USD was about 1.3390 at 21:30 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has climbed as US tech shares fell and traders trimmed dollar positions
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3392 at 10:00 Dubai to about 1.3432 at 15:00 Dubai on Friday. Amazon and Intel disappointed investors, Nasdaq futures fell about 2%, and buying of US Treasuries pulled yields lower, which weakened the dollar; ING also pointed to traders reducing dollar positions before Tuesday's midterm elections. ING described the move as led by the dollar, since there was no UK data, and swaps markets were pricing a Bank of England rise on 5 November as fully expected, which gives the pound support.

feed.title: The dollar has weakened despite strong US growth figures
feed.text: On Thursday US growth came in at 3.4% against 3.2% forecast, core inflation (PCE) rose 0.3% in September as expected, and jobless claims were 194,000 against 198,000 forecast. Figures like these usually firm up a Fed rise and lift the dollar, yet the odds of a December rise fell from about 84% to about 70%, according to FXStreet, as traders trimmed their bets. GBP/USD rose from 1.3326 to 1.3335 within ten minutes, slipped to 1.3313 by 17:00 Dubai, then climbed from 1.3332 at 18:15 Dubai to 1.3375 by 19:20 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has held steady overnight as oil eased on talk of Iran diplomacy
feed.text: Brent slipped to $114.10 (about £85.70) at 07:48 Dubai, down from a close of $115.32 (about £86.60) on Wednesday, after the Wall Street Journal reported that Vice President JD Vance had written to Iran's National Security Council chief to revive peace talks, though President Trump said he had not directed the letter. Cheaper oil tends to soften the dollar, but FXStreet read Chair Warsh's tone on Wednesday as firmly hawkish, which supports it, and the two roughly cancelled out. GBP/USD stayed between 1.3301 and 1.3335 through the night and was about 1.3311 at 12:39 Dubai, against 1.3321 at the last update.

feed.title: Sterling has peaked and eased back as Warsh's briefing ended
feed.text: During the press conference Chair Warsh said the committee's policy is starting to work some but there are no firm conclusions, and that he is unwilling to call financial conditions tight; Yahoo Finance reports the dollar slipped against the euro while he spoke, though no report ties the move to one remark. GBP/USD rose from 1.3299 at 22:30 Dubai to a high of 1.3337 at 22:43 Dubai, and EUR/USD rose in step (1.1136 to 1.1163), so this was the dollar easing rather than news about the pound. The pound then slipped back to about 1.3321 by 23:39 Dubai as the US ten year yield returned above 5% and traders still priced about an 85% chance of a Fed rise on 9 December, which tends to support the dollar.

feed.title: The Fed has held rates, with two members voting for a rise
feed.text: The Fed kept its range at 3.75% to 4% as expected, but Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack voted for a quarter point rise, and the statement upgraded growth to a strong pace while dropping its earlier wording on bringing inflation back to 2%. Two votes for a rise keep a December increase in view, which supports the dollar, though the ten year Treasury yield rose only from about 5.02% to 5.04%. GBP/USD rose from 1.3298 to about 1.3310 within two minutes, then settled near 1.3293 by 22:24 Dubai; the jump to 1.3370 on Kraken at 22:01 was a single stray trade, not a real move.

feed.title: Sterling has edged up during Chair Warsh's press conference
feed.text: Chair Kevin Warsh opened by saying activity is expanding at a strong pace, inflation remains elevated and the committee will deliver price stability. GBP/USD rose from 1.3294 at 22:32 Dubai to about 1.3320 by 22:36, and was about 1.3323 at 22:40. No report read so far names the remark behind that rise, so the cause is not yet clear.

feed.title: Sterling has edged up as the dollar eased before the Fed
feed.text: GBP/USD dipped to 1.3295 at 19:49 Dubai, rose to a high of 1.3320 at 20:55 Dubai and was near 1.3308 at 21:39 Dubai. EUR/USD moved the same way, from 1.1131 to 1.1149 and back to 1.1140, so this was the dollar softening a little rather than news about the pound. No source names a cause for the move; FXStreet reports that traders are waiting for the Fed's decision at 22:00 Dubai, where a hold is expected.

feed.title: Sterling has edged up as the Budget passes without a shock
feed.text: The Chancellor, John Healey, told the Commons that the Office for Budget Responsibility puts headroom against the borrowing rules at £15bn in 2029/30, down from £23.6bn in March but in line with forecasts, and the 10 year gilt yield eased from 5.355% to 5.344%. A Budget that calms the gilt market tends to support the pound, and GBP/USD rose from 1.3290 at 17:25 Dubai to 1.3304 by 17:40 Dubai, slipped back to 1.3289 at 18:15 Dubai, then climbed to a high of 1.3311 at 19:20 Dubai and was near 1.3303 at 19:35 Dubai. EUR/USD barely moved (1.1131 to 1.1135), so the gain was the pound firming rather than the dollar weakening; ING describes the reaction in gilts and sterling as small.

feed.title: The Budget is under way, with little effect on sterling so far
feed.text: The Chancellor began his first Budget at 16:30 Dubai, and the Office for Budget Responsibility's forecasts, including the headroom against the borrowing rules, follow the speech. In the first ten minutes GBP/USD dipped from 1.3291 to 1.3288 and was back at 1.3293 by 16:39 Dubai, while EUR/USD held near 1.1133, so neither the pound nor the dollar has moved on the news yet. Ebury expects headroom of about £15bn and ABN AMRO says a figure below £14bn could unsettle gilts, so a larger cushion would tend to support the pound and a smaller one would tend to weigh on it.

feed.title: Sterling has held steady in the hours before the Budget
feed.text: GBP/USD has traded in a narrow band since late morning, rising from 1.3289 at 11:44 Dubai to 1.3297 at 12:30 Dubai, easing to a low of 1.3275 at 15:00 Dubai and recovering to 1.3288 by 15:39 Dubai, while EUR/USD barely moved (1.1124 to 1.1125), so neither the pound nor the dollar has had fresh news. FXStreet reports that markets are waiting for the Budget at 16:30 Dubai, with UK public debt above £3 trillion in September and jumpy gilt markets, and that the dollar is supported by caution before the Fed's decision at 22:00 Dubai, where a hold is expected and the question is whether Chair Warsh backs a rise in December.

feed.title: Sterling is near a two week low ahead of the Budget and the Fed
feed.text: GBP/USD touched 1.3275 in the last hour and was 1.3289 at 11:44 Dubai, down from 1.3373 at Friday's close, as the dollar has firmed all week against the euro as well as the pound, and the pound has also slipped a little against the euro this morning. Today brings the two biggest events of the week: the UK Budget at 16:30 Dubai, where a plan that calms the gilt market would tend to support the pound and one that worries it would weigh on it, and the Fed's decision at 22:00 Dubai with Chair Warsh speaking at 22:30, where a hold is expected and a firm signal of a December rise would tend to lift the dollar.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped further on Budget morning
feed.text: GBP/USD eased from 1.3303 at 07:40 Dubai to a low of 1.3285 at 10:36 Dubai, its fourth day of losses, with the last step from 1.3292 to 1.3286 in the two minutes after 10:30 Dubai. The pound also lost ground against the euro (EUR/GBP rose from 0.8363 to 0.8370) while EUR/USD slipped only from 1.1126 to 1.1120, so most of this fall was the pound weakening and a smaller part was a firmer dollar. FXStreet points to caution before the Chancellor's first Budget at 16:30 Dubai, where tight borrowing limits and high government borrowing costs leave him little room, and to a dollar steadied by caution before the Fed's decision at 22:00 Dubai; no single news item this morning explains the latest step.

feed.title: The dollar has stayed firm overnight ahead of the Budget and the Fed
feed.text: GBP/USD drifted from 1.3312 at 20:40 Dubai last night to a low of 1.3301 at 05:49 Dubai and was near 1.3303 at 07:40 Dubai, while EUR/USD eased by a similar share, from 1.1131 to 1.1126, and the pound did not move against the euro, so this was the dollar holding near a two week high rather than news about the pound. FXStreet reports no single news item behind it, pointing to caution before the UK Budget at 16:30 Dubai and the Fed's decision at 22:00 Dubai, and to rising bond yields around the world, which tend to support the dollar.
